title: Bridging Simulation and Silicon: A Study of RISC-V Hardware and FireSim Simulation
problem: RISC-V ISA is emerging for HPC, but simulation tools lack validation against real hardware. FireSim is powerful but its prediction accuracy for physical RISC-V systems is not systematically evaluated. Gap between simulated and measured performance remains unclear.
motivation: MILK-V Pioneer (first desktop-grade RISC-V system) enables HPC evaluation, but architectural simulation for design space exploration requires validated tools. FireSim promises scalability but needs empirical validation for RISC-V platforms.
method: The researchers built simulations of two real RISC-V computers—a commercial single-board computer called MILK-V Pioneer and a desktop RISC-V CPU—using FireSim. They ran the same performance benchmarks on both the real hardware and in the simulation to compare results. They tested both single-core and four-core configurations using different workloads, including small test applications and LAMMPS (molecular dynamics simulation software).
key_novelty: This work provides the first systematic validation of FireSim's accuracy by comparing its simulations directly to real RISC-V hardware.
contributions: First systematic evaluation of FireSim prediction accuracy for RISC-V hardware
Measurement of performance discrepancies between simulated and real RISC-V systems
Identification of limitations in simulation fidelity
Evaluation of HPC workloads (LAMMPS) on RISC-V platform via FireSim

metrics.simulation_fidelity: Accuracy of simulated vs. measured runtimes

limitations: Restricted CPU specification availability hampers precise configuration matching; discrepancies remain unexplained; limited discussion of scalability beyond 4 cores; unclear if findings extend to HPC-specific architectures.
